title: Pixel-art kit: ramps, auto-shaded sprites, dither, pixel-perfect canvas
summary: shadeSprite(rows, ramps) lights and outlines a letter-map sprite (top-left light, selective outline, white hit-flash copy; scale 2 for twice the detail, scale 4 for four times: round corners and smooth nine-shade light); ramp(base) makes a hue-shifted 5-shade ramp; RAMPS ready-made; dither/bayer; pi

title: Pixel effect player: any of 244 effects on a canvas or a three.js texture
summary: playFx(id, {palette, seed, flip, angle}) loads one effect on demand and returns a player: update(dt), canvas, origin, size, done, stop(), texture(THREE). Find ids with `npm run kb -- <words>` (kind pixel-effect).

title: Sprite baker: 3D models rendered once into 2D sprite sheets
summary: SpriteBaker renders skinned models (soldier ranks, skeletons, robot) from a three-quarter camera into sheets — 5 directions (mirrored for 8), idle/run/walk/attack frames — plus still objects; then the 3D is let go. The classic pre-rendered sprite look at 2D cost.

title: Realistic 2D land: photo-textured bands, cliffs, blight, depth-sorted sprites
summary: paintLand paints a whole map once (texture bands blended on noise masks, piled-boulder cliffs, walls, scattered props); drawWorld draws shadows then everything back to front; remains() leaves bones and rubble on the land.

title: Synthesized game sound and adaptive music (Web Audio)
summary: PurgeAudio: effects built from shaped noise and tones (shots, blasts, horn, bell, coins, frost) through a compressor and a short reverb; a step-sequenced score (chords, bass, melody, kick/snare/hats, arpeggio) with calm and battle beds that cross-fade on a fight level; music and sound switches.

title: Headless RTS-style simulation with rooms
summary: Purge: fixed-step sim with spatial hash, grid A* with corner cutting, group move formations, guard camps that wake and leash, spawners, waves, bunkers, upgrades, bots; snapshot() small enough to send 10×/s; host-run rooms via MobaLink + Mirror interpolation.

title: Shared HUD overlay for 2D and 3D views
summary: drawOverlay/pickAt/boxedIn work with any view exposing toScreen(x,y,z): health bars, names, popups, box-select, picking — so a game can have a 2D and a 3D view of one simulation.

title: Cover-shot script: real screenshots of every game
summary: scripts/covers.mjs opens each game in a browser, stages a good moment, hides HUD and saves an 800×450 JPEG to public/covers.

title: Asset catalog: query models and materials by theme and kind
summary: Catalog.query/pick over library/catalog.json (KayKit, Poly Haven, ambientCG, extras), with categories and themes; everything that places a model goes through it.

title: Race courses planned on a real road graph
summary: buildGraph + planCourse/planRun: Dijkstra with a heap over OSM roads, used-edge penalty, spur and hairpin cutting; deterministic so every player plans the same course.

title: Animation retargeting bone by bone
summary: Borrow one rig's idle/walk/run for another skeleton: each bone's turn from rest copied across in each skeleton's own frame.

title: Pixel-perfect rendering: draw small, zoom by a whole number
summary: Paint the world on a low-resolution canvas (K=2 detail pixels a world unit) and copy it up at an integer zoom with imageSmoothingEnabled=false. Never 2.5×: uneven scaling makes some pixels wider — the commonest reason pixel games look cheap. Round every draw position and the camera (after shake) to

title: Colour ramps with hue shifting
summary: Each material gets 5 shades, deep shadow to highlight; shadows shift towards blue-violet and highlights towards yellow instead of only darker/lighter. A palette of 24–40 colours in ramps of 4–5.

title: One light source, top-left, everywhere
summary: Top and left edges take lighter shades, bottom and right darker, on every sprite, tree and rock. The lower part of a shape is a shade darker.

title: Selective outlines, not black
summary: Each outline pixel is the darkest shade of the colour it touches mixed towards a deep ink; top edges get a lighter outline than bottom edges, which reads as rim light.

title: Dithering only on big shapes
summary: A 4×4 Bayer pattern blends two shades without a new colour: add the Bayer value before choosing the shade. Use on grass, shadows and large shapes — never on small sprites, where it reads as noise.

title: Silhouette first
summary: Block the character in one flat colour: if it reads as a dark shape it reads in the game. Big heads, hats and eyes; a 1-pixel white glint in each eye. Judge at real size and speed, never zoomed in.

title: Keep text out of the pixel layer
summary: Damage numbers, labels and the HUD are drawn at full resolution on top (or in the DOM), so they stay sharp at any zoom.

title: Paint the ground once
summary: Paint terrain, decorations, contact shadows under trees and sun patches into one big offscreen canvas at load; copy from it each frame. Painting is slow, copying is free.

title: Y-sorting and a shadow pass
summary: Everything that stands (trees, enemies, the player) goes in one list sorted by foot position each frame; draw all shadows first, then sprites in order, so you can walk behind a tree.

title: Every action answers: flash, number, shake, particles
summary: A hit gets a sound, a white flash (a pre-made pure-white copy of the sprite for 0.1 s), a damage number and knockback; big actions get screen shake (decaying fast) and particles; small ones get neither.

title: Additive blending for light, normal for matter
summary: Fire, glows and flashes use globalCompositeOperation='lighter' so overlaps add to white-hot cores; smoke, dirt and debris use normal blending. Fire colour follows a particle's age: white-hot to deep red.

title: Cast time sells power
summary: A 0.45 s wind-up with a growing magic circle and the caster slowed makes the explosion feel earned. Area hits on a ground seen at an angle are ellipses: divide the vertical distance by ~0.6.

title: Colour grade and vignette last
summary: Three final passes set the mood: a soft-light warm fill over the pixel layer, a slow breathing sunbeam gradient in screen mode, and a radial vignette.

title: Rules for a good pixel effect
summary: Lines and light, not fills; hard ramp steps in colour, softness only in light and smoke; fast in, slow out with a 1–2 frame white hero frame; vary every particle; light from one side; let one-shots shrink or dither out; loops seamless; seeded, never Math.random; under 2 ms a frame.

title: Pixel-art pass for 3D scenes (general palette, transparent, detail 1–4)
summary: pixelPass(renderer, { detail: 4 }) draws any three.js scene as pixel art: inked edges, ordered dither, snapped to a 64-colour palette built from our ramps; see-through background; detail 1 chunky … 4 fine.

title: Flow-field navigation per body size
summary: One clearance grid; a Dijkstra cost field per body-size class seeded round the target, at most one field rebuilt per frame; each mover walks downhill to the furthest cell in plain sight, then bends its heading onto obstacle tangents. Cheap for hundreds of chasers.

title: Wave director on a point budget
summary: budget(w)=9+3.2w spent on a weighted enemy pool by cost; split into groups sent on an interval or when the field is empty; max-alive cap; boss every 5th wave with the rest at 55%; party size scales foes and life.

title: Fixed pool of point lights
summary: Eight PointLights made once; flash() takes a free one or steals the oldest, fades by life, can follow an object. The light count never changes, so no shader ever recompiles mid-game.

title: Instanced skinned crowds
summary: Every creature of a kind is one instanced draw: joint matrices and per-body looks (dissolve, frozen, hit flash, rim colour) are rows of a float texture read with gl_InstanceID, injected through onBeforeCompile.

title: Cloth with position-based dynamics
summary: Rings of particles (28×7), verlet at 60 Hz with 3 iterations of distance constraints (ring, down, shear, bend), a tether to the top ring and a capsule collider for the arm. Works for sleeves, capes, banners.

title: Verlet ragdolls
summary: Bodies handed to a small verlet solver on death: points, stick constraints, ground contact, then written back to the bones.

title: SDF sculpting meshed with surface nets
summary: Shapes as signed distance fields (smooth unions), meshed once with surface nets, textured triplanar, skinned with dual quaternions so joints do not collapse.

title: Weapon swing trails
summary: A ribbon through Catmull-Rom points sampled from the blade tip and base each frame, fading along its length, additive.

title: Pooled CPU particles
summary: Fixed-size pools drawn as one instanced mesh or points; emit() overwrites the oldest; no allocation while playing.

title: Frame pacing and auto quality
summary: Measure frame time over a window; step a quality preset down or up with hysteresis; change only what needs no shader change.

title: Sound design that carries on laptop speakers
summary: Weight goes in the mids, not sub-bass: cut under 120 Hz after the drive stage; a blow needs 0.3 s of decay to read as a blow; spells play no notes (they clash with the music); one generated hall reverb whose noise darkens as it decays; crackle textures from random impulses.

title: World labels drawn in WebGL
summary: Damage numbers, names and bars painted into one canvas atlas and drawn as a single instanced batch, not DOM nodes.

title: See-through walls and line-of-sight blackout
summary: Screen-door dissolve of whatever stands between the camera and the hero; a 360° sight polygon blacks out what the hero cannot see.

title: Shaders compiled at load, never mid-game
summary: Every material variant is rendered once off-screen at load and pinned; loading is cut into short chunks; heavy textures are made in workers.

title: Bank-or-risk loot
summary: Loot found in a run stays in a bag until banked between waves; dying forfeits the bag; rarity weights rise each wave.

title: Deterministic fixed-tick simulation
summary: Fixed 20 Hz, a seeded generator, never reads render state, the clock or Math.random. The same seed and commands always give the same game, so saves, replays, rewinding, lockstep play and headless tests all come from one sim.

title: Lockstep multiplayer with a desync hash
summary: Only commands cross the wire; each runs at tick T+delay (delay adapts 2–15 ticks); a relay closes each tick; clients compare a hash of the state every so often; trig functions replaced by portable versions so engines agree to the last bit.

title: Replays you can scrub and take over
summary: Store seed + command stream + periodic hashes; scrub by re-simulating from the nearest snapshot; watch through any player's fog; "take command" starts a new game from that moment.

title: Grid A* with generation counters
summary: 8-connected, no corner cutting; visited/closed arrays stamped with a search number instead of being cleared; remembers the nearest reachable cell as a fallback; path smoothed by line-of-sight string pulling.

title: Formations that keep their shape
summary: A virtual centre walks one path; slots laid out in rows (line, box, wedge), sorted by role with armour in front and by current side so nobody crosses; blocked slots squeeze towards the centre; the group waits for stragglers.

title: Fog of war with a soft, drifting edge
summary: The sim stamps circles into visible/explored grids; the renderer eases them into a texture (visible 5/s, explored 3/s) and the ground shader samples it with a noise offset: fogged = desaturated cool tint, shroud = dark clouds with a faint rim.

title: Trauma screen shake
summary: trauma 0..1 rises with kicks and decays steadily; amplitude = max × trauma^1.3, scaled by camera distance; the offset is a sum of two unrelated sines per axis; reduced-motion sets it to zero.

title: Game-feel director
summary: One place owns shake, a "clash" meter fed by nearby fighting that drives music intensity, and brief slow-motion on big moments.

title: Procedural models as one skinned draw
summary: Build a model as a node tree; every node with body geometry becomes a bone and all body parts merge into one skinned mesh (one draw call); turrets and doors move by moving bones; ambient occlusion, edge wear, snow and mud baked into vertex colours; a far LOD body.

title: Vertex-animation-texture crowds
summary: Animation clips baked into a texture (one row per frame, one column per vertex); thousands of instanced soldiers play and cross-fade clips in the vertex shader.

title: GPU particles
summary: Positions and velocities live in float textures stepped by a ping-pong pass; 8k–64k particles in one draw, colliding with a terrain height texture.

title: Hundreds of lights without THREE.Light
summary: Lights binned into a screen-tile grid and applied in one full-screen pass; muzzle flashes and explosions each get one.

title: Buildings that break apart
summary: Pre-cut a building into Voronoi chunks bound to bones of one skinned mesh; a small rigid-body solver drops them; craters scar the ground texture.

title: Gerstner water and ship wakes
summary: Sum of Gerstner waves for the surface; Kelvin-V wakes drawn into a texture behind each ship.

title: Weather in a camera-following volume
summary: Rain and snow are a fixed box of points round the camera, wrapped and animated in the vertex shader; lightning bolts by midpoint subdivision.

title: Landmarks and towns from a grammar
summary: A small kit (walls, storeys, roof types) plus rules builds whole towns; landmarks are hand-written recipes on the same kit.

title: Fair map generation
summary: Generate one sector and mirror it for symmetric skirmish maps; check path lengths and resources per start, re-roll if unfair.

title: Skirmish AI without cheating
summary: Sees only what its fog shows; a personality vector (aggression, greed, tech) weights choices; plans operations (harass, push, defend) and counters what it has scouted; named rivals remember how you played.

title: Seeded adaptive music
summary: Three layers (calm, build, battle) cross-faded by an intensity 0..1; sections generated from tables of progressions, kick/bass/lead rhythms; lead melody = a motif walked in scale degrees, snapped to chord tones on strong beats, varied over four phrases; stingers in the current key on the beat; sched

title: Sound effects rendered once, offline
summary: Each effect is a recipe (pitched thump + crack + filtered noise + metal partials) rendered in an OfflineAudioContext with a generated reverb, normalised, kept as buffers in a few variations; one recipe takes a size 0..1 from pistol to howitzer; a mixer steals voices by priority.

title: RTS controls on mouse, touch and pad
summary: Box select, control groups, layout-aware keys; touch: hold-then-drag selects, radial menu, pinch/twist camera; pad: virtual cursor and radial menu.

title: 3D globe campaign map
summary: One shader draws spherical Voronoi territories from a lookup texture of the nearest sites; a 2D canvas overlay carries badges; battle odds computed exactly.

title: Accessibility for games
summary: Colour-blind-safe team palettes (Okabe–Ito), subtitles for sounds, reduced motion, UI scale, no large flash faster than ~1.5 a second.

title: Talking 3D avatar as a web component
summary: A custom element that loads a rigged GLB, plays an idle (breathing, blinks, glances), drives mouth morph targets from audio loudness or visemes, and retargets animations between skeletons by bone-name maps.

title: Entity-component-system layout
summary: Entities are ids; components are plain arrays per type; systems are functions run in a fixed order over queries; scenes are data. Keeps game rules, rendering and UI apart.

title: Pixel-perfect camera
summary: Render the world at a fixed low resolution and scale by a whole number; snap the camera to whole pixels and carry the remainder as a sub-pixel offset of the final blit so scrolling stays smooth.
